items.title: Curtis Fuller — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He and Jim Hall had a duo thing going on you know?

ctx.x: So let’s talk about the issue around that Jazztet, it’s cooperative nature, and how that evolved. And then, how that was affecting what your ambitions were.

You have to understand, now Art Farmer had the same problems I had. On his own, he would work with Jim Hall a lot, just he and Jim Hall. He and Jim Hall had a duo thing going on you know? It was brilliant, you know? They worked nice together. I would like to do that and it was like more financially suitable

because, you know… At that time, he had moved to Austria and he could take a few bucks home. The Jazztet, you know, every time the band moved Benny had us on tour with his daughter and his wife and everybody else. That took a lot away from what the band made. Art would speaks me about that
